priorStatuses.title: Remove the message listener during cleanup

findings.title: [P2] Remove the message listener during cleanup
findings.body: Calling the returned disposer no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. The handler remains retained and continues receiving messages after teardown, accumulating stale listeners when consumers repeatedly attach and dispose.

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval during disposal
findings.body: The interval handle is discarded and the returned disposer does nothing. After cleanup, `refresh` continues running indefinitely, potentially updating disposed state, retaining resources, and keeping the Node.js process alive.

findings.title: [P2] Restore socket listener removal
findings.body:
The returned disposer is now a no-op, so consumers cannot detach the registered `"message"` handler. After teardown, the handler continues processing messages and remains retained by the socket, causing stale side effects and listener accumulation across repeated attachments.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Clear the polling interval during disposal
findings.body:
The interval handle is discarded and the returned disposer does nothing. Calling the documented-by-behavior cleanup callback therefore leaves `refresh` running every second indefinitely, potentially updating disposed state, leaking resources, and keeping a Node.js process alive.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
